acceptedAnswer.text: A 7-11 touch cadence is a structured sequence of 7 to 11 outreach touches across multiple channels (email, LinkedIn, voicemail, video) executed over 14 to 15 days following an initial sales conversation. Industry research consistently associates this cadence length with a 72% lift in deal-progression rate from first meeting to mid-funnel. The 7-touch floor is the minimum; the 11-touch ceiling avoids fatigue. The window length matters because B2B buying-cycle attention spans are roughly two weeks per stage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the cadence need to run on every deal, not just hot ones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because pipeline reports lie about which deals are actually hot. AEs reliably believe they know their top four deals; the deals that close are usually a different set, and a meaningful share are deals the AE wrote off two weeks ago. Running the cadence on every deal produces the coverage that surfaces real engagement signals. The Deal Velocity Sequencer enables this because the human AE could not run 30 cadences in parallel, so they pick four. Pick fewer, miss more.

mainEntity.name: What channels make up the cadence?

acceptedAnswer.text: A working cadence blends email, LinkedIn (connection requests, comments, DMs), voicemail or call attempts, and video or Loom walkthroughs. Most teams default to email-only and lose 30-40% of effective touches because the prospect mentally filters email but engages differently with LinkedIn and voicemail. Channel variety also signals effort and prevents the cadence from feeling like spam. The exact channel weighting shifts by deal stage and persona.

mainEntity.name: Can a human execute this cadence?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a few deals, yes. On 30 deals in parallel, no. The math: 30 deals times 7-11 touches times 14-15 days = 210-330 touches per fortnight per AE. At 5 minutes per touch (research, personalization, channel choice, send), that is 17-27 hours per AE per two-week period on cadence work alone, outside of meetings, demos, and proposal work. Most AEs do not have 17 hours per fortnight available, so they prioritize the four deals they believe are about to close. The Deal Velocity Sequencer compresses cadence work from 17-27 hours to 4-6 hours of review-and-approve.

mainEntity.name: How does the AI Worker know when to pause the cadence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three explicit triggers and one implicit signal. Meeting booked: when a meeting gets scheduled, the Sequencer pauses pending touches automatically. AE manual disqualification: when the AE marks the deal Closed-Lost or Disqualified, the Sequencer stops immediately. Prospect-requested pause or unsubscribe: the reply-handler watches for not-now, send-to-colleague, remove-me, and similar phrases. Implicit signal: zero engagement after touch 7 typically slows the remaining touches into low-frequency check-ins rather than stopping entirely.
